prompt: A medication has a half-life of $6$ hours: every $6$ hours, half of the remaining amount leaves the body. If a patient takes $80$ milligrams, how many milligrams remain after $24$ hours?
hint: The amount is cut in half once per half-life. Start by counting how many half-lives pass during the given time.

hints.text: The amount is cut in half once per half-life. Start by counting how many half-lives pass during the given time.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try one halving at a time: $100$ mg with a $2$-hour half-life is $50$ mg at $2$ hours and $25$ mg at $4$ hours. The exponent counts halvings, not hours.
Since $24 \div 6 = 4$, the amount is halved four times. Begin at $80$ milligrams and halve it step by step.
The amounts go $80$, $40$, $20$, $10$, $5$, so $5$ milligrams remain after $24$ hours.

learningObjective: Apply repeated halving over a fixed number of half-life periods.
explanation: Count the half-lives in the time given: $24 \div 6 = 4$, so the amount is halved four times.
Halving four times in a row gives $80 \to 40 \to 20 \to 10 \to 5$.
The formula agrees, since $80\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{4} = \dfrac{80}{16} = 5$. After $24$ hours, $5$ milligrams remain.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the halvings, not the hours
steps: The most common error is using an exponent of $24$ instead of $4$.
The exponent counts *periods*, and the number of periods is elapsed time divided by the half-life.
Writing "$24 \div 6 = 4$ halvings" as your first line makes the exponent impossible to get wrong.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Using 24 as the exponent gives an astronomically small number; using 6 gives another neat wrong answer.
The exponent counts halvings: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 of them. Write that division as your first line and the rest is four clean halvings.
